text: [American Motorists Ins. Co. v. Allied-Sysco Food Services, Inc. (1993) 19 CA4th 1342, 1351, 24 CR2d 106, 110-111 (disapproved on other grounds by Buss v. Sup.Ct. (Transmerica Ins. Co.) (1997) 16 C4th 35, 65 CR2d 366)] (a) [3:471] Compare—where covered “offense” alleged: On the other hand, humiliation damages may be recoverable where employment discrimination is joined with claims of an “offense” covered under “personal injury liability”: e.g., defamation, malicious prosecution, invasion of privacy, etc. [See American Guarantee & Liab. Ins. Co. v. Vista Med. Supply (ND CA 1988) 699 F.Supp. 787, 794 (applying Calif. law)—insurer owed duty to defend claim that employer had falsely accused employee of dereliction of duty, humiliating her in front of others: i.e., a potential defamation claim that would be covered under the policy] (2) [3:472] (Nonstandard) definition including “discrimination”: Some nonstandard CGL forms define “personal injury” to include discrimination claims.
